extracted.intended_audience: bank holding companies and applicants under Regulation Y; interested commenters and potential hearing requesters; regulated entities and counsel (also FTC respondents and parties subject to premerger notification)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for submitting comments or requesting a hearing on Federal Reserve Regulation Y applications (section 4(c)(8) acquisitions) and related Federal agency orders/notices (including premerger early termination and FTC final orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing request contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for a hearing on this question must be accompanied by a statement of the reasons a written presentation would not suffice in lieu of a hearing, identifying specifically any questions of fact that are in dispute, summarizing the evidence that would be presented at a hearing, and indicating how the party commenting would be aggrieved by approval of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must explain why oral hearing is necessary (written comments not adequate); specifically identify disputed factual issues; provide a summary of the evidence that would be offered; and state how approval of the proposal would cause aggrievement to the requester. This statement is required to support a hearing request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission deadline and location
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments regarding the application must be received at the Reserve Bank indicated or the offices of the Board of Governors not later than [specified date].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are case-specific (examples on this page: January 24, 1990 and January 18, 1990). Comments must be filed at the Reserve Bank listed in the notice or at the Board of Governors. Timely filing by the deadline is a procedural requirement for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 4(c)(8) 'closely related to banking' test
rubrics_metrics.description: A bank holding company may engage in any activity which the Board has determined to be 'so closely related to banking or managing or controlling banks as to be a proper incident thereto.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An activity may meet the test if demonstrated that: (a) banks have generally provided the proposed activity; (b) banks generally provide services operationally or functionally so similar to the proposed activity as to equip them particularly well to provide it; or (c) banks generally provide services so integrally related to the proposed activity as to require their provision in a specialized form. The Board may also consider any other basis demonstrating a reasonable or close relationship to banking (citing National Courier Ass'n v. Board of Governors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public benefits vs adverse effects balancing for 'proper incident to banking'
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether an activity meets the 'proper incident to banking' test, the Board must consider whether performance of the activity by an affiliate can reasonably be expected to produce benefits to the public, such as greater convenience, increased competition, or gains in efficiency that outweigh possible adverse effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible adverse effects to weigh include undue concentration of resources, decreased or unfair competition, conflicts of interest, or unsound banking practices. Applicants should address both potential benefits and possible adverse effects in their submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application authority and scope under Regulation Y
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to acquire or control voting securities or assets of a company engaged in a nonbanking activity listed in §225.25 of Regulation Y must be filed under §225.23(a)(2) or (f) and §225.21(a) of Regulation Y, relying on section 4(c)(8) of the Bank Holding Company Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities listed in §225.25 are those the Board has identified as closely related to banking and permissible for bank holding companies; notifications and filings must follow the cited Regulation Y provisions and are available for inspection at the Reserve Bank and Board offices once accepted for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible data processing services conditions (§225.25(b)(7) example)
rubrics_metrics.description: To engage in providing data processing and data transmission services, facilities or databases to others as a permissible nonbanking activity, three conditions must be met: (i) the data to be processed or furnished are financial, banking, or economic, and the services are provided pursuant to a written agreement so describing and limiting the services; (ii) the facilities are designed, marketed, and operated for the processing and transmission of financial, banking, or economic data; and (iii) the hardware provided in connection therewith is offered only in conjunction with software designed and marketed for the processing and transmission of financial, banking, or economic data, and where the general purpose hardware does not constitute more than 30 percent of the cost of any packaged offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three prongs (data-type and written agreement limitation; facility design/marketing/operation; hardware/software packaging and <=30% general-purpose hardware cost) must be satisfied for the activity to fall within §225.25(b)(7). Applications should explicitly show conformity to these conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on prior Board rulings and adherence to limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may rely on the Board's prior determinations (e.g., Morgan, Bankers Trust, PNC Financial Corp.) that similar activities are closely related to banking, but must commit to abide by the limitations imposed in those orders and any applicable existing limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating adherence to conditions and limitations from precedent decisions (including any specific behavioral or structural restrictions) supports approval and helps address concerns about adverse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hart-Scott-Rodino early termination publication practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 7A(b)(2) of the Act permits the agencies to terminate the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period prior to its expiration in individual cases and requires that notice of such action be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When early termination is granted by the FTC and DOJ, the agencies publish the transactions granted early termination in the Federal Register; the published table names acquiring persons, acquired entities, PMN numbers, and dates terminated. Neither agency intends to take action on the listed proposed acquisitions during the waiting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'title search and examination services' (FTC matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Title search and examination services' means all activities which are designed to identify and describe the ownership of a particular parcel of real property as well as any other actual or potential rights to, encumbrances on, or interest in the property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definitional standard governs the scope of services covered by the Commission's order and related prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on collective rate-setting through rating bureaus (FTC final order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each respondent is ordered to cease and desist in specified states from discussing, proposing, setting, or filing any rates for title search and examination services through a rating bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition is geographic (New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Wisconsin, Arizona and Montana in this order) and covers any direct or indirect activity, including actions through corporations, subsidiaries, divisions or other devices, in connection with the sale of title search and examination services affecting commerce as defined by the FTC Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-action exception (FTC order carve-out)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the FTC Order shall prohibit respondents from collectively setting or adhering to prices for title search and examination services in any state where such collective activity is engaged in pursuant to clearly articulated and affirmatively expressed state policy and where such collective activity is actively supervised by a state regulatory body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify for the state-action carve-out, (1) there must be a clearly articulated and affirmatively expressed state policy authorizing the activity, and (2) the collective activity must be actively supervised by a state regulatory body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance, notice, and reporting obligations (FTC order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each respondent must, within thirty days after service of the Order, deliver a copy of the Order to all present officers, directors, and personnel having responsibility in determining company prices and to the commissioner of insurance in each state listed; notify the Commission at least thirty days prior to corporate changes that may affect compliance (dissolution, assignment, sale, successor, creation/dissolution of subsidiaries); and within ninety days file with the Commission a written report detailing the manner and form of compliance, and at such other times as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely delivery of the Order, advance notice of corporate changes affecting compliance obligations, and detailed compliance reports are mandatory obligations; failure to comply can be enforced by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of applications and documents for inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is available for immediate inspection at the Federal Reserve Bank indicated, and once accepted for processing it will also be available for inspection at the offices of the Board of Governors. Copies of FTC complaints, initial decisions, opinions and statements are available from the Commission's Public Reference Branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested persons and commenters can inspect relevant application materials at the indicated offices, which supports public participation and informed comment.
